RIDER: Your fare for this trip was reviewed and we found you were charged for extra distance on two stretches where the route taken didn't match the best route for your trip. The trip ran 27.5 km against a 15.9 km optimal route, and 10.79 km of that extra distance wasn't explained by any incident, road closure or agreement with you. We're issuing a Ryde voucher of $15.21 for the extra kilometres. Nothing else changes on your account.

DRIVER: We reviewed the fare for this trip. The route driven was 27.5 km against a 15.9 km optimal route, adding 11.6 km. On two stretches the extra distance was not matched to any incident or road condition, and no route change was agreed with the rider in the trip chat, so those kilometres are not payable. A Ryde voucher of $15.21 will be issued to the rider for 10.79 km of extra distance. Your account is not being flagged and this does not affect your standing.

First segment, 21:46–21:56: 6.98 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.04 km, adding 6.94 km (F3). RD-4(a) is marked ✗: no incident is matched to the replaced stretch, and a speed band (F12, F13) cannot exempt a segment under RD-4(b)/(c) [F3][F12][F13][F14][RD-4]. RD-5 gives no relief, and this I can decide from the record rather than leaving it undetermined: the chat is complete and every message is timestamped (F10), and it contains only the rider's 21:33 pickup note and the driver's 21:34 arrival note (F8, F9) — neither names any road, area or route, and neither is an agreement to a diversion. RD-3 is inapplicable: no stop was measured in this segment and no rider message named a place (F8, F9) [F3][F8][F9][RD-3]. The segment therefore counts and its 6.94 km are refundable [F3][RD-2].

Second segment, 22:04–22:13: 5.92 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.07 km, adding 3.85 km (F4). No incident is matched to this stretch either; the only speed records are band 4 on the PIE and band 5 on the KPE (F12, F13), which under RD-4(b) are corroboration only and cannot stand alone, so RD-4(c) sends the segment to RD-2 [F4][F12][F13][RD-4]. RD-5 again gives no relief on the same complete, timestamped chat (F8, F9, F10) and the same non-consent statement (F11) [F4][F8][F9][F10][F11][RD-5]; RD-3 is inapplicable for the same reason [F4][F8][F9][RD-3]. This segment counts [F4][RD-2].

Amount: RD-2 for RydeTAXI refunds the extra kilometres of the unexempt segments at the trip's per-kilometre rate, i.e. fare.distance_fare ÷ fare.distance_km = $38.80 ÷ 27.5 km = $1.4109/km, consistent with the $1.41/km rate in F5 [F4][F5][F7][RD-2]. Unexempt extra km = 6.94 km (F3) + 3.85 km (F4) = 10.79 km; 10.79 km × $1.41/km = $15.2139 ≈ $15.21 [F3][F4][F5][F7][RD-2]. The award is not zero, so no_action is unavailable, and the refund issues as a Ryde voucher under NS-7 [RD-2][NS-7]. Because the trace marks both RD-4(a) screens ✗ and the first segment's basis includes the earlier-vetoed concession that had rested only on F14, I flag for the reviewer that the per-segment allocation is the residual interpretive point; the arithmetic ceiling on the totality of deviating kilometres is as computed above.

claims.assertion: The trip was a RydeTAXI metered service billed on distance and time (F7: base $3.90 + distance $38.80 for 27.5 km + time $10.86 for 41.8 min = $55.03), so the extra kilometres the driver drove entered the fare paid by the rider.
The driver drove 27.5 km against an optimal 15.9 km, +11.6 km (+73%), and took 41.8 min against an estimate of 21 min (F1, F2), so the driver did not take the shortest and most direct route.

The GPS track shows two off-route segments: 21:46–21:56, where 6.98 km was driven where the optimal route covers 0.04 km (adding 6.94 km, up to 2240 m off route), and 22:04–22:13, where 5.92 km was driven where the optimal route covers 2.07 km (adding 3.85 km) (F3, F4).

Neither segment is exempted by consent: the only chat messages are the rider's pickup note at 21:33 and the driver's arrival note at 21:34 (F8, F9), both sent before the trip, and neither mentions or agrees to any route change; the rider's complaint also states she never agreed to any change.
The driver's post-trip claim of an unavoidable accident diversion (F11) is a statement, and his post-hoc narrative is not consent by the rider for RD-5 purposes.

Traffic evidence justifies only one of the two segments at most: the accident reported at 21:26 on the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway lies 0 m from the optimal route with lanes blocked (F14), but that exemption can cover no more than the first deviation window (21:46–21:56, F3); the second segment 22:04–22:13 (F4) has no incident supporting it, and the only speed records are moderate bands on PIE and KPE (F12, F13), which under RD-4 are corroboration only and cannot stand alone.

The rider is therefore entitled to a partial refund of the unexempt off-route kilometres: the segment F4 added 3.85 extra km and, if the first segment is treated as exempt, the excess billed for that segment is 3.85 km × the $1.41/km rate evidenced in the fare breakdown (F5), i.e. $5.43; in the alternative, if the first segment is also found unexempt, the refund is 6.94 + 3.85 = 10.79 km × $1.41 = $15.21.
The driver's account shows 447 trips in 90 days with 1 dispute upheld, and although that profile alone cannot decide the case, it supports adding an account-review flag if the deviation is upheld.

weaknesses: F14 shows a genuine accident at 21:26 on the KPE, 0 m from the optimal route with lanes blocked, so the driver's story in F11 is partly corroborated and the first off-route segment (F3, 21:46–21:56) is likely exempt under RD-4(a) — that alone removes 6.94 km from my refund calculation.

The 11.6 km / 73% excess in F1 and the $16.41 excess-distance figure in F5 include both segments; the judge may find the whole detour explained by the KPE incident and the residual 0.25 km map-matching slack, which would reduce the award under RD-2 to $0 and force no_action.

The second segment (F4, 22:04–22:13) is not supported by any incident in the traffic record, but I have no direct evidence of what the driver did off route there, and F13's speed band 5 could be argued as traffic pressure on the return leg.
The chat record (F10) is complete but contains no route discussion at all, so there is no message from the rider refusing a change — I rely on the absence of consent rather than an express objection.
The rider's own profile (F16) shows 2 disputes in 90 days with 0 upheld, which the other side may use to suggest a pattern of unsuccessful complaints.

claims.assertion: The first deviation (21:46–21:56, +6.94 km, F3) is justified: an LTA-reported accident on the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway (towards Tampines Mall) with lanes blocked was reported at 21:26 — before the segment began — and sits 0 m from the optimal route, which is the very road the optimal route uses (F14, F13). This is the 'reasonable cause' route the policy contemplates for a reroute, and at most only the portion not covered by the accident evidence should be scrutinised.

The rider never once complained in-app about the route: the complete, fully timestamped chat record (F10) contains only a pickup greeting at 21:33 and the driver's arrival message at 21:34 (F8, F9). Nothing in the record shows the rider objecting or the driver ignoring a routing request, so this is not the 'changing route without passenger's permission' situation the guideline targets.

There was no surge: multiplier 1.0× (F6). The extra distance in the meter is therefore attributable to the metered distance units, not to any price manipulation, and the driver made no manual add-on beyond the printed breakdown of base $3.90, distance $38.80, time $10.86, platform $1.47 (F7).

Against the profile, the driver shows no history of upheld route-deviation findings: 447 trips in 90 days, 2 disputes, only 1 upheld and route: 0 (F17). If the tribunal finds any residual deviation, the refund should be limited strictly to the non-exempt distance at the metered rate and no account flag is warranted on this record (RD-6 threshold of a prior upheld route dispute is not met).

weaknesses: The GPS record is the strongest evidence against us: +11.6 km / +73% (F1), 41.8 min vs 21 min (F2), and especially F3 — 6.98 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.04 km, up to 2240 m off route — which the other side will say cannot be explained by one accident on one expressway.

The second segment F4 (+3.85 km, up to 931 m off route) is not covered by the accident incident's location (F14 sits on KPLEx, 0 m from the optimal route); the driver's written statement (F11) offers no traffic evidence specific to that segment, and under RD-4(b) a speed band alone (F12, F13) is only corroborative and does not by itself exempt a segment.

There is no pre-deviation consent in the chat: the rider's complete message set (F8, F10) contains no agreement to any reroute, and any verbal-agreement claim in F11 is a statement, not consent under RD-5/G11 — so the deviation cannot be defended as agreed.

Under RD-2 the refund is formula-based and not a matter of discretion: if any segment is upheld as non-exempt, the rider's entitlement is Σ(extra_km) × $1.41/km (F5, F7), so 'no action' may be untenable and we are, at best, arguing about which segment amounts remain.

points.response: We do not contest that the first segment is exempt: the accident reported at 21:26 on the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway, 0 m from the optimal route with lanes blocked (F14), was reported before the segment began (F3, 21:46), so that segment falls under RD-4(a). This concession reduces our claim to the second segment only.

The second segment (F4, 22:04–22:13, +3.85 km, up to 931 m off route) is not covered by the accident, which is matched to the KPE corridor (F14) rather than to whatever road the driver took at 22:04; the only other traffic evidence is speed band 4 on PIE and band 5 on KPE (F12, F13), which RD-4(b) says is corroboration only and cannot exempt a segment on its own, so under RD-4(c) that segment must be handled under RD-2.

Silence is not consent: the complete, timestamped chat (F8, F9, F10) contains no message from the rider agreeing to any route change before either segment started, and RD-5 requires the rider's own message sent before the deviation — the absence of an objection cannot supply it.

We accept there was no surge and no undisclosed add-on (F6, F7); our case is not price manipulation but the metered consequence of unexempt mileage, which RD-2 makes refundable precisely because the RydeTAXI meter charges the extra kilometres actually driven.

We withdraw the account-flag request: the driver's profile shows route: 0 upheld route disputes (F17), so the RD-6 predicate of a prior upheld route deviation is not met on this record, and the remedy should be limited to the refund.
Claim C8 is withdrawn for the reasons in our answer to D5.

Correct on the mechanism, but the amount is the issue: only unexempt metres enter the fare, and the $16.41 excess figure (F5) is not itself the refund — RD-2 refunds per unexempt segment's extra_km at the $1.41/km rate (F7), so the rider's own arithmetic concedes the exempt segment's 6.94 km is not hers.

The +11.6 km / +73% headline (F1) and the 41.8 min (F2) are aggregates of both segments, and the policy's own obligation is qualified — RD-1/RD-4 excuse a deviation where there is reasonable cause, which the traffic record supplies for the corridor the driver was told to avoid (F14, F13).

Both segment figures are accepted as recorded — driver does not dispute the GPS (F3, F4) — but the finding they support is that each segment was a reroute away from the KPLEx corridor, whose accident was reported at 21:26 and still listed with lanes blocked across the whole trip window (F14).

Concede: the complete, timestamped chat (F10) contains only F8 and F9 and no rider consent to any route change, so the driver cannot claim RD-5 exemption — the case turns entirely on the RD-4 reasonable-cause branch, not on agreement.

The driver does not put F11 forward as consent; it is offered only as the reason for the reroute, and the reason is independently corroborated by the LTA accident entry (F14) rather than by the statement.

Partly conceded, but the second segment is not left bare: the accident at 0 m from the optimal route (F14) forced traffic onto the PIE/KPLEx corridor recorded at speed bands 4 and 5 for 21:27–22:24 (F12, F13), i.e. the same congestion persisted through the 22:04–22:13 window, and under RD-4(b) that band data is corroboration supporting the reasonable-cause finding for the continuing reroute.

The $5.43 figure is accepted only in the alternative and is the ceiling, not the outcome: 3.85 km × $1.41 = $5.43 (F4, F7), and if the tribunal accepts the continuing-congestion evidence for the second segment (F12, F13, F14) the correct action on both segments is no_action under RD-4(a), with at most the residual map-matching slack excluded by RD-2.

The profile does not reach the RD-6 trigger: the driver's 90-day record shows 1 dispute upheld with route: 0 (F17), so there is no prior upheld route-deviation finding to make this case 'repeated', and the flag is unavailable on this record.

If the tribunal does not accept the congestion corroboration for the 22:04–22:13 segment, the driver does not contest an award capped at $5.43 (3.85 km × $1.41/km, F4, F7) — the only magnitude supported by the segment facts — and asks that no account flag accompany it (F17, RD-6).
